title: Fleet autoscaler: enforce hard min/max bounds + safety checks + decision/audit logging
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Dedicated Autoscaling: customer bounds + predictive signals
content:
Context / problem
Dedicated pools are currently scaled via a mostly reactive control loop. This has caused two classes of customer pain (see SUP-4821 / Slack incidents):
1) Unexpected spend due to scale-up beyond what customers consider an acceptable cap.
2) Scale-down/scale oscillation and/or aggressive scale-down that increases latency / throttle risk.

This ticket implements the autoscaler-side enforcement of customer-configured min/max bounds, plus guardrails and structured decision logs so we can:
- Guarantee “hard max” (never exceed customer max)
- Enforce “min floor” when feasible, while respecting drains/maintenance/shortage semantics from ADR-0142
- Make scaling decisions explainable (audit trail + metrics with cardinality controls)

Scope (in)
- Clamp computed desired replicas within evaluated bounds from policy engine:
  - desired = clamp(desired_unbounded, effective_min, effective_max)
- Add safety checks on computed desired (NaN/inf/negative/huge jumps)
- Emit structured decision logs (“scaling decision events”) that include:
  - unclamped desired, clamped desired, effective min/max
  - reason(s) for clamp, and key inputs used to compute desired
  - config revision/evaluated-policy hash so we can correlate decisions to config changes
- Integration tests covering:
  - hard max never exceeded
  - min honored in steady state (when no drains/shortage)
  - drain/maintenance interactions
  - actuation failures and retries do not cause bound violations

Scope (out)
- UI/Console surfacing of the audit trail (tracked in ENG-2847)
- Predictive signal blending (ENG-2845); this ticket must not assume forecast is present
- Feature flag/allowlisting mechanics (ENG-2848) beyond plumbing any required config toggle fields

Assumptions / inputs
- Bounds semantics are defined in ADR-0142 (max is strict; min is best-effort under certain conditions).
- The autoscaler consumes an evaluated config from policy engine (ENG-2842), not raw customer config.
- Replicas == “GPU slices/instances” at the pool scaler level; treat as integer.

Implementation plan
1) Autoscaler decision flow
- Current (simplified):
  - desired_unbounded = computeDesiredFromSignals(pool_metrics, queue_depth, util, latency, etc.)
  - desired_applied = reconcile(desired_unbounded)
- New:
  a) Fetch evaluated bounds:
     - effective_min_replicas
     - effective_max_replicas
     - enforcement_mode (expected values: hard_max, best_effort_min)
     - reason metadata (e.g., “min relaxed due to drain/maintenance”)
  b) Compute desired_unbounded as today
  c) Validate desired_unbounded:
     - if NaN/inf -> fallback to current_replicas (no-op) and log safety_violation
     - if < 0 -> set to 0 and log
     - if > ABSOLUTE_MAX_REPLICAS (internal guardrail) -> cap and log (protects fleet)
  d) Clamp:
     - desired_clamped = min(max(desired_validated, effective_min), effective_max)
     - Clamp reasons are additive (list): ["above_max", "below_min", "invalid_input", "fleet_guardrail"]
  e) Rate limit (existing):
     - ensure we don’t request > max_scale_up_step per tick and > max_scale_down_step per tick
     - NOTE: rate limiting happens AFTER bounds; rate limiting must not cause us to exceed max.
  f) Actuate:
     - reconcile to desired_applied
     - if actuation fails, ensure retry logic does not “drift” above max due to stale state

2) Hard max invariant
- Invariant: applied_replicas <= effective_max MUST hold across:
  - normal scaling
  - retries on failed actuation
  - manual interventions (if operator pins > max, autoscaler should not scale further up; logging should show "pinned_above_max" for visibility; follow-up ticket if needed)

3) Min semantics (best-effort)
- Normal mode:
  - applied_replicas >= effective_min
- Exceptions:
  - When policy engine indicates min is relaxed (e.g., maintenance drain / region shortage), autoscaler may operate below min. This must be visible in logs with "min_relaxed" metadata.

4) Decision/audit logging
- Emit a structured log event once per reconcile tick per pool (sampled if necessary later; start at 1:1 for allowlisted pools only).
- Proposed fields (keep stable + low-cardinality):
  - pool_id, region, hardware_class
  - timestamp
  - current_replicas
  - desired_unbounded
  - desired_validated
  - effective_min, effective_max
  - desired_clamped
  - applied_replicas (post actuation attempt)
  - clamp_reason (enum string; if multiple, join with "+" in log field; metrics will use a bounded set)
  - decision_inputs_summary (compact string: queue_depth_bucket, util_bucket, latency_bucket; avoid raw values in log index; raw values ok in debug-only logs)
  - evaluated_policy_version / config_revision
  - enforcement_mode
- Coordinate with ENG-2846 for metrics; this ticket focuses on logs/events, but should include the hooks and stable enums.

5) Testing
- Unit tests:
  - clamp() behavior including edge conditions
  - validation fallback behavior
  - “hard max” property (property-based test: random desired_unbounded, random min/max, ensure clamp output within range)
- Integration tests (simulated controller loop):
  - steady-state scaling with min/max
  - scale-up attempts beyond max due to bursty queue depth => clamped
  - scale-down attempts below min => clamped
  - actuation failure: desired stays within bounds on retries
- Log schema tests:
  - ensure required fields are present and clamp_reason is one of allowed enums

Acceptance criteria
- Autoscaler never emits an actuation request above effective_max for an allowlisted bounded pool.
- Autoscaler never emits an actuation request below effective_min when enforcement_mode is normal (no drain/shortage), aside from transient reconciliation ordering within one tick.
- Each reconcile tick emits a decision event containing min/max, unclamped desired, clamped desired, clamp_reason, and evaluated config revision.
- Integration test suite covers both “above max” and “below min” scenarios.

Links
- ADR-0142 autoscaling bounds semantics (Confluence)
- ENG-2841 control plane schema (min/max fields)
- ENG-2842 policy engine evaluation output
- ENG-2846 observability metrics for scaling decisions
- GitHub: PR redwood/pr-21905 (this change)

Open questions / follow-ups
- If operators pin replicas above max for incident mitigation, should autoscaler actively scale down to max or just stop scaling up and warn? (Default for now: do not fight manual pin; surface log "manual_pin_detected" and leave as-is. Create follow-up if product wants stricter behavior.)
- How to handle multi-region pools where effective bounds may be per-region vs global? For v1, treat bounds as per-pool per-region evaluated values; policy engine is responsible for producing per-region effective_min/max.

Progress / updates
2026-01-18 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Created ticket after SUP-4821 escalation: customer reported spend exceeded expected cap; agreed "hard max" needs to be enforced in fleet controller (not just UI).

2026-01-22 (Keiko Yamamoto)
- Drafted implementation plan: clamp after computing desired and after input validation; keep rate limits after clamp.
- Started adding a structured decision event (JSON log) with stable enums for clamp_reason.

2026-01-26 (Jordan Lee)
- Policy semantics note: max is always strict; min is best-effort when policy engine indicates drain/maintenance/shortage. Make sure autoscaler consumes effective bounds (not raw) and logs enforcement_mode.

2026-01-29 (Allison Grant)
- Observability review: avoid high-cardinality in metrics. OK to log raw values to debug logs but decision events should bucket inputs or keep them as "summary" strings.
- Requested clamp_reason enums be kept small + stable for dashboards.

2026-02-03 (Keiko Yamamoto)
- Implementation complete locally with unit tests. Added integration test harness for actuation failure path.
- Noted potential interaction: cooldown + clamp could cause repeated no-op cycles; flagged for monitoring during dogfood.

2026-02-06 (Vanessa Ortiz)
- Fleet review: added internal ABSOLUTE_MAX_REPLICAS guardrail to prevent runaway if bounds missing/invalid. This is an internal safety net and should never be hit for evaluated-config pools.

2026-02-07 (Keiko Yamamoto)
- Opened PR redwood/pr-21905: "Fleet autoscaler clamps desired replicas within bounds and emits structured decision logs".

2026-02-10 (Rafael Mendes)
- SRE sign-off contingent on:
  - explicit invariant test for never exceeding max on retries
  - decision logs include evaluated config revision
  - add runbook pointer (ENG-2851) once Console surfaces it

2026-02-11 (Keiko Yamamoto)
- PR merged. Ticket marked Done.
- Post-merge note: during staging we observed a cooldown/clamp corner case leading to “stuck at min” symptoms; hotfix tracked separately (see PR-22057 / SUP-4965).
